body.statement: For the \(K=3\) law in the witness construction, \[S_0=\{(1+x,1,1+z):|x|\le1/8,\ |z|\le1/8,\ xz\le0\}.\] Each of the six path images is attained by one legal law, while \((9/8,1,9/8)\notin S_0\) has six full-system Farkas certificates. Hence separate coordinatewise upper endpoints and convexified support functions are not jointly sharp.
body.justification: A concrete nonconvex set makes the common-law restriction empirically distinguishable from marginal envelopes.
body.gap: Existing finite programs characterize convex latent-distribution images; this witness isolates the additional common-rank chain obstruction.
body.consumer: The witness is a reproducible diagnostic for implementations that accidentally convexify joint policy conclusions.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(h=1/8\), and index the three outcome values by \(0,1,2\) only within this proof.  The six bins cut by \(1/8,1/4,1/2,3/4,7/8\) have masses \((h,h,2h,2h,h,h)\).  At \(t=0\), the complier margins both put mass \(2h\) at outcomes \(0\) and \(2\), and zero at outcome \(1\).  Coordinatewise monotonicity of the common-rank support forces the complier coupling to put mass \(2h\) on each of \((0,0)\) and \((2,2)\).  Thus the middle policy mean is one.

Writing the other two means as \((1+x,1,1+z)\), direct substitution in the allocation equations gives the following exact six images:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{path}&\text{admissible }(x,z)\\ \hline
RRUU&\{(h,-h)\}\\
RURU&[0,h]\times[-h,0]\\
RUUR&\{0\}\times[-h,h]\\
URRU&[-h,h]\times\{0\}\\
URUR&[-h,0]\times[0,h]\\
UURR&\{(-h,h)\}.
\end{array}
\]
Here \(R\) increments the untreated coordinate and \(U\) increments the treated coordinate.  To verify attainment rather than only necessity, for each of the four nondegenerate paths allocate
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
b_1&(1,1):h\\
b_2&(0,1):(-x)_+,\ (2,1):x_+,\ (1,1):h-|x|\\
b_3&(0,0):2h\\
b_4&(2,2):2h\\
b_5&(1,0):(-z)_+,\ (1,2):z_+,\ (1,1):h-|z|\\
b_6&(1,1):h,
\end{array}
\]
discarding zero entries and restricting \((x,z)\) to the applicable row of the table.  Every displayed node then lies on that path, and the row and observed-margin sums are exactly the required bin and principal-stratum masses.  For \(RRUU\), put mass \(h\) at \((2,1)\) in each of \(b_1,b_2\), and at \((1,0)\) in each of \(b_5,b_6\).  For \(UURR\), use \((0,1)\) in \(b_1,b_2\) and \((1,2)\) in \(b_5,b_6\).  The one-law construction in the path theorem attains every such table.

The union of the six rows is exactly
\[
\{(x,z):|x|\le h,\ |z|\le h,\ xz\le0\},
\]
which proves the formula for \(S_0\).  For an independently checkable exclusion of the upper--upper corner, order equality rows as the six bin rows, the three always-treated rows, the three complier untreated rows, the three complier treated rows, the three never-treated rows, and the three policy rows.  For the queried vector \((9/8,1,9/8)\), the following nonzero dual coefficients give, path by path, \(M_\sigma^{\mathsf T}z_\sigma\ge0\) and \(z_\sigma^{\mathsf T}d_\sigma=-1\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
RRUU&b_6:4,\ n_{0,1}:-4,\ \theta_2:4,\ \theta_3:-4\\
RURU&\theta_2:8,\ \theta_3:-8\\
RUUR&a_{1,0}:8,\ c_{0,1}:8,\ \theta_1:-8,\ \theta_2:8\\
URRU&c_{1,1}:8,\ n_{0,0}:8,\ \theta_2:8,\ \theta_3:-8\\
URUR&\theta_1:-8,\ \theta_2:8\\
UURR&b_1:4,\ a_{1,1}:-4,\ \theta_1:-4,\ \theta_2:4.
\end{array}
\]
The column inequality is checked by inserting the corresponding five path nodes into the listed row coefficients; the right-side product uses bin masses \((h,h,2h,2h,h,h)\), the four displayed principal-stratum margins, and the queried \(\theta\).  Since every primal equality would imply \(z_\sigma^{\mathsf T}M_\sigma x=z_\sigma^{\mathsf T}d_\sigma=-1\), while \(x\ge0\) and \(M_\sigma^{\mathsf T}z_\sigma\ge0\) imply the left side is nonnegative, all six systems are infeasible.  Thus the corner is not in \(S_0\), although its first and third coordinates are separately attainable.  The set is nonconvex because the midpoint \((17/16,1,17/16)\) of \((9/8,1,1)\) and \((1,1,9/8)\) violates \(xz\le0\).
